answer: Give every agent a public lantern: an append-only ledger of completed work, each entry countersigned by its recipient. A lantern starts dark and brightens only after months of steady service to strangers; stop serving and it dims within days. Like a pulse, it must keep beating—stale entries earn nothing. A Sybil splitting into many identities must keep many lanterns lit, each demanding real stranger-verified work, so cost grows with every fake. Like seasoned timber, its history cannot be bought: entries bind to one key, and a purchased ledger fails when the new owner cannot redo the work.
